name: Planar Biped
summary: Marc Raibert's two-legged running machine — the first robot to run on two legs. Two telescoping legs, each a hydraulic actuator working in series with a pneumatic air spring, hang from pivot hips on an aluminium body constrained to a plane by a boom. Its insight was that a biped can be controlled as a one-legged hopper by designating one active leg at a time, so the same three rules — hopping height, forward speed, body posture — produce running.
notable: First robot to run on two legs (1985), and to change between one- and two-legged gaits
Did flips and aerials in 1986 — the first robot gymnastics
Reached 13.1 mph (1989), selected footholds on rough terrain and climbed a stairway
Ran before any robot could walk dynamically: balance first, then gait
